title: [Feature][Attention] Port tested FlashMLA integration onto merged PROLOG main
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Port external FlashMLA decode onto main, using the reviewed v0.30.0 integration from #18758 at `d1aa5a515` with the required main request-state and graph-dispatch adaptations. This revision replays the existing 11 PR commits individually onto main `ccaf14ad31`, preserving their original authors, author dates, commit messages, co-authors and sign-offs, and adds one test/release-note commit.

- Eligible MRv2 MLA decode uses `flash_mla` / `flash_mla_metadata`; real prefill remains on FIA. Cache allocation, guarded PROLOG writes and reads use the matching token-fused KV layout.
- Ordinary DCP decode reads full rank-local KV in one call. Speculative causal decode retains history/current attention and exchange/combine. Current KV/Q staging precedes the auxiliary-stream ready event.
- The backend owns metadata refresh, captured buffers, request ordering and restrictive decode-graph eligibility. The runner retains the parent gather result and invokes the conditional FlashMLA helper before derived inputs and graph dispatch.
- Preserve main's removal of obsolete PD prefill reclassification. Resolve the PROLOG conflict with main #19213 by using `tile_size=128`, independently of writer cache page size, while retaining this integration's writer workspace and scatter behavior.
- Adapt the new main tile-size test fixture to the writer workspace interface without removing assertions. Add 16 API-contract combinations and the release note fragment required by current repository guidance.
- CI workflow files have no PR-specific changes. The previous temporary E2E shutdown workaround remains reverted.

The query-boundary None guard, generic builder request interface, PD layout validation and FP16 writer eligibility remain follow-ups.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible MRv2 configurations select FlashMLA decode, including DCP/DSpark and supported PD connectors. PROLOG uses its supported tile attribute for non-128 writer pages. This revision does not introduce the later BF16-only selection restriction or Mooncake MLA shape guard; PD endpoints must use compatible cache layouts and configurations.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ten related CPU test files: **684 passed, 4 existing skips**, using CI-pinned vLLM `c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b` and `VLLM_VERSION=0.31.0.dev0`.
- New tile-size regression covers 128/768 writer pages, FlashMLA on/off, KV quantization modes 0/1 and query quantization on/off. Against the previous PR source, four ordinary-FIA 768-page cases fail and twelve pass; the corrected source passes all sixteen. API checks preserve cache identities, shapes and slot mappings.
- Retain all existing PD prompt-tail, graph-gate, dummy-batch, DCP and PROLOG assertions, including the new main tile-size regression.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` and diff whitespace checks passed on this candidate.
- Isolated reproductions of the existing ordinary `git rebase` step pass against both adopted main `ccaf14ad31` and observed newer main `3abf581d36`. The latter result's complete tree equals a normal merge with that main. This replaces the previous snapshot/rebase blocker; it is not a claim that all remote CI has passed.
- The only production-code difference from previous PR head `4231e9cb86` is the fixed PROLOG tile attribute and explanatory comment. Original 11 commit author records and trailers were checked individually after replay.
- No new NPU execution, graph replay, PD E2E, GPQA or performance validation was run. Remote results must be assessed on this exact head.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab
